You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_target.csv: 284 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, whose rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) is AS CLOSE AS POSSIBLE
to 800. Design variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
I propose retaining the composition and processing of the **718 MPa sample**, but lowering its tempering temperature (`TT`) from 490 to **415.5**.

The data support this direction: for several fixed compositions, lowering `TT` increases fatigue strength. For example:
- With C=0.57, Si=0.30, Mn=0.82, strength rises from 425 to 486 to 533 MPa as `TT` decreases from 650 to 600 to 550.
- With C=0.44, Cr=1.05, Mo=0.21, strength rises from 516 to 578 to 625 MPa over the same temperatures.

These examples suggest approximately **1.1 MPa additional strength per unit decrease in `TT`**. Anchoring that trend to the 718 MPa sample gives:
\[
\widehat{\text{strength}}=718+1.1(490-415.5)\approx800\ \text{MPa}.
\]

This is an extrapolation of the temperature response for that particular composition, not a validated 800 MPa measurement. Nevertheless, it preserves an observed composition and processing route rather than mixing the substantially different processing regimes on either side of the 718–900 MPa data gap. All proposed values satisfy the supplied bounds.

Final: NT=845, THT=845, THt=30, THQCr=8, CT=30, Ct=0, DT=30, Dt=0, QmT=30, TT=415.5, Tt=60, TCr=24, C=0.62, Si=0.29, Mn=0.88, P=0.026, S=0.007, Ni=0.05, Cr=0.75, Cu=0.12, Mo=0.03, RedRatio=796, dA=0.058, dB=0, dC=0.004
